meta.title: Claims-to-capital operating backbone
meta.note: Every operation is marked at one of three levels. The claim being made is about where the line sits, not that the line can be removed.

levels.label: Autonomous
levels.definition: Runs without a human in the path. Deterministic, verifiable, and cheap to re-run. A human audits the output, but nothing waits on one.

levels.label: Human-in-the-loop
levels.definition: The system does the work and proposes a result. A human confirms, corrects, or rejects before it moves downstream. The work is drafted, not decided.

levels.label: Human
levels.definition: Stays with a person. The system may assemble the record and surface the considerations, but the judgment and the accountability do not move.

operations.label: Ingest and schema normalization
operations.does: Reads loss runs and register extracts in whatever shape they arrive, maps them onto the program's canonical schema, and normalizes dates, statuses, and coverage codes.
operations.why: Purely mechanical and fully checkable. The mapping is deterministic, and every transformation is reversible to the source row.

operations.label: Identity and entity resolution
operations.does: Detects the same claim arriving under different identifiers, and the same insured arriving under different spellings. Proposes merges.
operations.why: Auto-merging a near-match claim number is exactly as dangerous as leaving the duplicate. High recall, no autonomy: every proposed merge is held for confirmation.

operations.label: Policy year and coverage assignment
operations.does: Assigns each claim to a policy year and coverage part from occurrence and report dates against the coverage basis.
operations.why: Rule-driven from the policy terms. Claims-made and occurrence bases are unambiguous once the dates are clean — and the dates were cleaned upstream.

operations.label: Coverage issue identification
operations.does: Reads the claim file against the policy form and surfaces the provisions in play, the facts that bear on them, and the open questions.
operations.why: The retrieval and assembly are reliable. The weighing is not. It produces the memo a coverage analyst would have spent three hours assembling, and stops there.

operations.label: Coverage determination
operations.does: Decides whether the claim is covered, in part or at all, and on what terms.
operations.why: A coverage position is a legal judgment the carrier will be held to. It does not move, and no efficiency argument should move it.

operations.label: Erosion and development computation
operations.does: Tracks paid and incurred against the per-occurrence retention and the annual aggregate, and builds the development triangle.
operations.why: Arithmetic on reconciled data. The only failure mode is bad input, which is why intake carries the exception gate.

operations.label: Case reserve setting
operations.does: Proposes a case reserve from claim characteristics and the development pattern of comparable claims.
operations.why: The adjuster knows things the record does not — venue, counsel, how the plaintiff presents. The proposal anchors, the adjuster decides.

operations.label: IBNR and ultimate projection
operations.does: Applies chain-ladder factors derived from the program's own triangle to project each policy year to ultimate.
operations.why: The method is standard and the factors are derived, not asserted. Judgment enters only through the tail factor, which is exposed as an explicit input rather than buried.

operations.label: Funding requirement calculation
operations.does: Converts projected ultimate liabilities and the target capital margin into a required funding position by quarter.
operations.why: Deterministic given the projection and the margin policy. Both inputs are visible and adjustable.

operations.label: Funding trigger and capital call
operations.does: Decides whether to call capital, adjust the funding schedule, or restructure at renewal.
operations.why: It moves money and it involves the parent. The system's job is to make the number defensible early enough that the decision is not made under time pressure.

operations.label: Invoice review against billing guidelines
operations.does: Checks counsel invoices line by line against the billing guidelines — block billing, staffing ratios, rate changes, duplicate entries, non-billable tasks — and proposes the adjustment.
operations.why: Flagging a line against a written rule is mechanical. Short-paying a firm is not: it is a contract position and a relationship decision, and a system that takes it unattended will eventually take it wrong against counsel you need. The review runs on every line; the deduction waits for a person.

operations.label: Counsel assignment and strategy
operations.does: Selects counsel and sets litigation strategy and settlement authority.
operations.why: Relationship and judgment, informed by performance data the system can supply but should not act on.

operations.label: Board memo drafting
operations.does: Assembles the quarterly capacity memo — position, movement, projection, exceptions — with every figure linked to the rows that produced it.
operations.why: The assembly is mechanical and the narrative is templated from computed values. A human owns it before it goes out, and traceability is what makes that review possible in an hour instead of a week.

operations.label: Board decision
operations.does: Approves the renewal structure, the funding position, and the capacity plan.
operations.why: Always. The entire point of the traceability is to make this decision better informed, not to make it somewhere else.
